Given: The reader is in history on the primary conversation at a narrow viewport, and Automations covers the transcript.
When: They Alt-click a side conversation in the chat list, opening it alongside the primary conversation and dismissing Automations.
Then: The primary conversation remains at its route with the side conversation selected in the sidebar query, and the empty side conversation shows capability discovery. The original reading anchor is restored; subsequent image growth and incoming replies preserve its screen position without returning to the tail.
finding: At 930 px, Alt-click selected Side survey alongside the original route and exposed discovery. The same primary text moved from y=469.25 to y=318.5 on opening the side panel. The pending and decoded Mermaid card above it measured 219 × 164.25 px in both controls. The receiver accepted the new reply, but the side layout did not expose marker 17.
nextEntry: Repeat if a production image can change its flow height in this side layout or the side-panel width/anchor restoration changes.

Given: The reader is in history with a visible message anchored in the transcript.
When: A late-loaded image above the messages increases content height by 75 pixels.
Then: The anchored message remains at the same screen position.
finding: The diagram started 693.5 px above the same visible text. With delivery withheld, and again after the HTTP image was released and the thumbnail decoded, the card measured 420 × 315 px and the text stayed at y=434.25. This supplies zero of the specified 75 px height change.
nextEntry: Use a flow image above that event whose rendered box demonstrably grows by 75 px.

Given: The reader reaches the tail, changes the live scroll offset to 275, and opens Automations at a narrow viewport.
When: A new reply containing a Mermaid diagram begins asynchronous image preparation, and the reader closes Automations before preparation finishes.
Then: The oldest message at the captured reading position remains at the same screen position while preparation is pending and after the diagram image is ready; the reader is not forced to the tail.
finding: At scrollTop 275, the oldest visible line (Turn 1, observation 2, event ending 000002) was at y=59.25 before and after closing Automations. A second reference, Question number 2, was at y=296. The new reply was received under the panel. Its image receiver saw zero requests while covered and after reveal. The first request arrived after scrolling to the tail, when the original text had left the mounted window; withholding and decoding then produced the same 420 × 315 px card.
nextEntry: Use an entry that starts preparation before closing Automations while the same oldest text is still measurable.

Given: Two registered tabs subscribe to the same user-channel topic.
When: The topic emits an event, the connection suspends and reconnects, then the first tab disconnects and another event arrives.
Then: Both tabs receive the first event; a plain resume causes no resync, while reconnect causes one resync per tab. After the first tab disconnects, only the second receives the next event, and the shared subscription ends after the second disconnects.
finding: Two independent Chromium Routers showed turn 17, then the surviving window showed turn 18 after the first closed. The provider identified the user and credential channels separately. In the separate billing-topic trial the account menu showed 0 credits after the balance fixture supplied 10,000, so that menu could not count refreshes. This chat publication does not establish the per-tab resynchronization count or final removal of a shared user-topic subscription.
nextEntry: Use a visible value on the same user topic in both tabs, identify both refreshes on a continuity gap, and obtain the final unsubscribe at the provider.

Given: A registered tab subscribes to presentationTemplatesChanged at organization scope.
When: An event is published on its organization's channel.
Then: The tab receives the event through that organization channel.
finding: The opened presentation shelf contained no Harbor exhibit before publication. The unrelated organization produced no card. The correct organization reached one provider callback for presentationTemplatesChanged. Two valid notifications produced no card in the already-open shelf. A fresh same-origin Router read the published catalog and did show Harbor exhibit, confirming the card and response fixture were valid.
nextEntry: Trace a publisher and downstream presentation shelf refresh that use the same organization scope, with a positive catalog-read control.

Given: Two registered tabs share an indicator read; the first tab's token is delayed and the second tab can provide a token immediately.
When: The second tab requests the indicators while the first token request is still pending.
Then: The read completes without waiting for the first tab and uses the second tab's bearer token. Both tabs receive token requests.
finding: The indicator HTTP receiver identified B while A’s external identity reply was held. Both identity sources were asked. A fresh B sidebar initially displayed its cached Side survey with no new indicator HTTP call. The B-authenticated HTTP read and visible Unread state followed the external notification. The ordinary B visit has yet to initiate that shared read while A is pending.
nextEntry: Require a fresh indicator read initiated in the healthy window during A’s delay and distinguish it from a Worker-owned notification refresh.

Given: Two registered tabs share an indicator read; one token provider is pending and the other can provide a token.
When: The pending provider's tab disconnects before the healthy provider returns its token.
Then: The read succeeds using the healthy tab's bearer token.
finding: Two signed-in Router windows received identity requests for a shared refresh. The A window closed with its provider still held. Only then was B released. The HTTP endpoint received the B bearer alias and B showed Side survey as unread while the A reply was still withheld.
nextEntry: The native suite asserts the ordering, recipient and visible unread state.

Given: Two registered tabs share an indicator read, and one token provider rejects while the other is pending.
When: The second token provider also rejects.
Then: The shared read rejects with AggregateError after every tab's token provider fails.
finding: A rejected at the identity boundary while B was held and B subsequently rejected. After both rejections, restoring the provider allowed a new turn to appear. The Router did not expose the aggregate error type from that particular shared read.
nextEntry: Use a supported consumer that distinguishes AggregateError after both providers fail from an individual rejection or a generic unavailable state.

Given: Two tabs are registered.
When: The first tab disconnects and the second performs a cache-only read.
Then: The first tab's port closes, while the second tab's read succeeds with an empty result and its port remains open.
finding: After the first window closed, the offline survivor followed the empty-conversation link. The route changed. The expected empty result was not independently identified on that offline visit. After reconnecting, the same window received a new turn. A tab-close event alone does not acknowledge a closed port.
nextEntry: Capture the empty result through a fresh cache-only consumer and the lifecycle receipt for the closed tab.

Given: A registered tab has an unread thread and chat-message notifications; catch-up initially fails with HTTP 500.
When: A message notification triggers warming, then a later notification arrives after catch-up recovers and a second row is available.
Then: The unread indicators remain readable during the failure, and the later warming makes both rows available in the cache.
finding: The primary unread thread remained unopened while a notification on a different thread triggered a catch-up that returned HTTP 500. Its sidebar still said Unread. After a second notification and successful catch-up, the browser went offline and opened that unread thread for the first time. Both new rows, 17 and 18, appeared. The server also rejected fresh row reads during the offline control.
nextEntry: The native suite asserts both rows after first opening the target offline.

Given: Two ports subscribe to the same realtime topic while its shared attach is pending.
When: The attach fails, then one port reacquires the subscription.
Then: Both subscriptions reject with the attach failure, and the failed topic is no longer subscribed. After reacquisition, a notification reaches the new subscriber.
finding: Two Routers opened while the organization provider attach was withheld. The provider returned 503. A new registration later received live chat turn 17. That later turn uses a different topic; neither of the two original subscription rejection results was exposed by the page.
nextEntry: Require both failed subscribers to surface the same failed attach, then reacquire that exact topic and observe its notification.

Given: A ready viewer in shared-wire mode disconnects, and recovery capture is acknowledged but its image is held.
When: The wall clock moves back one hour and more than 30 seconds of monotonic time pass, then the image is released and recovery retries.
Then: The viewer shows reconnecting and remains disabled until retry succeeds, then becomes usable.
finding: The external capture acknowledgement was read before the first image budget began. Moving wall time back one hour and monotonic time forward 30,001 ms caused a stop request and left the reconnecting viewer disabled. Releasing the old picture did not enable input. A separately held retry picture did, and the original page received new text.
nextEntry: The registered Router test covers the complete frozen sequence.

Given: A ready viewer has two tabs in the same window, and the original tab is usable in shared-wire mode.
When: The user selects the replacement tab while its first image is held past 30 seconds, then retries with another held image that also exceeds 30 seconds.
Then: Each timeout shows reconnecting without disabling the original tab; after the retry image is released and recovery completes, the replacement tab is usable and accepts input in its own session.
finding: An initial input reached the original page. For the replacement in that same window, two separately acknowledged captures each exceeded 30 seconds. Both produced a stop and Reconnecting with the original tab available. After the second retry, input reached only the expected replacement session.
nextEntry: The registered Router test covers the complete frozen sequence.

Given: A ready viewer has a replacement tab in the same window, and its capture acknowledgement and first image are held.
When: The capture acknowledgement is delayed 20 seconds, then the image remains held for more than 30 seconds.
Then: The viewer shows reconnecting without replacing its connection; after the image is released and recovery completes, the replacement page is usable.
finding: The peer withheld the replacement capture acknowledgement for 20 seconds. Once the acknowledgement was consumed, the viewer stayed out of Reconnecting through another 29,999 ms and requested a stop after two further milliseconds. The connection count stayed at one. Releasing the old image and completing recovery produced a usable replacement input receiver.
nextEntry: The registered Router test covers the complete frozen sequence.

Given: A ready viewer is paused and resumed with the original tab's first image held; capture cleanup is also held after the image deadline expires.
When: The user selects the replacement tab before releasing cleanup and the old image.
Then: The replacement page remains usable after both old operations are released and accepts input in its own session.
finding: The original capture was resumed and acknowledged with its image withheld. At the deadline its stop acknowledgement was held. Before either old operation was released the user selected the sibling and saw the usable page. The sibling’s session then received the typed text after both old operations were released.
nextEntry: The registered Router test covers the complete frozen sequence.

Given: A viewer is switching to separate-image mode while native startup is held, then the viewport is paused and shared mode is unavailable.
When: The browser binding changes and its descriptor arrives while paused; shared mode becomes available, then the viewport resumes.
Then: The replacement page becomes usable and accepts input in its own session after the old native operation is released.
finding: The user chose Separate image connection and its native hello was withheld. The off-viewport canvas paused and Shared connection was unavailable. A new assigned-window descriptor arrived while paused and made the shared choice available. After returning the canvas to view and releasing the old hello, the replacement window received the text and the original did not.
nextEntry: The registered Router test covers the complete frozen sequence.

Given: The browser is ready and a navigation request is sent without receiving its response.
When: The request passes its response deadline and recovery completes.
Then: The navigation request is sent exactly once; it is not replayed.
finding: The real remote Chromium committed Arrival 1 while its navigation acknowledgement was withheld. At more than 31 seconds and after recovery its HTTP receiver still had one visit and its document history ID was unchanged. A deliberate submission of the same URL through the same Router produced Arrival 2 and a distinct history ID. The regular suite also typed into the recovered page with the old reply withheld.
nextEntry: The native replay asserts both the first delivery and the deliberate repeat.

Given: The connector catalog contains Gmail, which supports provider authorization.
When: The user tabs to Connect Gmail and presses Enter.
Then: One authorization window opens at the Gmail authorization URL and one OAuth connection request is made. Closing the dialog closes the authorization window.
finding: Tab and Enter started one real OAuth attempt and opened one provider window per ordering. State digests joined the consent and local API denial callback to that same admission. Closing the directory first left the popup able to deliver the callback. Delivering the callback first also left the popup open after directory dismissal.
nextEntry: A product change specifying popup ownership after cross-origin navigation, or a later callback lifecycle that actually closes the original window, would change the conclusion.

Given: Model settings have loaded and the Connect account control is enabled, while subsequent billing and subscription responses are pending.
When: The user switches to Preference and then returns to Models.
Then: The Models heading and the no-accounts-connected message appear, and Connect account remains enabled.
finding: Preference → Models with both reads held displayed Use more models and Loading accounts…, with neither the empty-account message nor Connect account. Releasing billing first did not restore those controls; releasing the subscription displayed the returned member, including when billing was still pending. #37519 documents the new heading and requests reuse of resolved data on refresh.
nextEntry: A supported re-entry retaining confirmed account data through both outstanding reads, or a later product decision explicitly changing that behavior, is needed.

Given: The user has a draft in the Image composer and opens the Image shelf.
When: They paste an unsupported PDF, then import a valid WEBP image as a reusable style.
Then: The PDF is not attached and does not send a message; the draft remains and an Image removal control is present. The WEBP starts a reusable-template analysis and publish message containing the file, without selecting a generation template, and navigates to a chat.
finding: Pasting a PDF attached it to the Image composer, retained the draft and Remove Image control, and sent no message. Importing a valid WEBP through the style picker sent both identified files in the analysis/publish chat and no generation template. In the paired picker-only control the PDF was filtered and only the WEBP was sent. #39648 and #50365 cover the contextual file chooser, not a changed clipboard rule.
nextEntry: Revisit when the production clipboard contract for unsupported style files changes or when a real paste is rejected before attaching.
